OK. I'll start out by saying that, as a Cowboys fan, I am biased to an insane degree against the Eagles. That said, before the season began, I predicted Chip Kelly would be one of the first fired after the regular season. I was shocked when he was fired before the end of the regular season. However, his firing was inevitable.

Now, most people are going to point to his questionable personelle decisions. However, I personally think that the Chip Kelly era was doomed from the start.

It all comes down to something I like to call, "The Dennis Erickson Effect." I call it this because of former Seahawks Head Coach Dennis Erickson's own short-lived foray into the NFL. I originally was going to call it the Nick Saban Effect, but Saban had prior NFL experience, albeit as an assistant. Erickson worked better for this. It's quite simple: successful coach in college goes to the NFL, does a decent job his first year, but things quickly go downhill due at least partly to the coach not understanding that the NFL is a very different game. See also: Barry Switzer, Bill Peterson,Steve Spurrier, etc.

In Chip's case, it was partly the fact that his offense wouldn't work well in the NFL, and that he let his ego run wild after gaining personnel control. As others have pointed out, college coaches can be dictators because college players have few rights. Chip didnâ€™t understand that this wasn't the case in the NFL, hence, he was doomed to find out the hard way.

Finally, he got rid of a lot of playmakers, but failed to find adequate replacements. So, let's hope he doesn't drive any more teams into the ground.
My thoughts on the firing of Chip Kelly.

Alright I'll put my counter argument in here then

He went 10-6 his first two years with Reid's players. But clearly neither of those teams were at the same level as say the Broncos, Pats, Packers or Seahawks. They were all a very clear tier two team that wouldn't really contend for a SB

So he blew it up and made big moves. Two teams have done this to almost the exact situation that I'm going to mention

First is the McDaniel's Broncos. Josh was given GM rights and made some very questionable news. He undoubtedly flopped on getting rid of Cutler and taking Tebow. But his first year there he went 8-8 and didn't see the same talent that his former team, the Patriots, had on their roster. He decided to make big changes and drafted and free angencied the shit out of that team. They went 4-12, the Broncos panicked and they fired Josh and reddit has circlejerked ever since. But what people fail to realize is that team immediately went to the playoffs right after. The team that Josh put together. The O-line was full of talent and the receivers had the best prospects in the league. The defence had players but was missing a few key pieces. The next season Peyton comes and they dominate for the next few years. Josh McDaniel's extremely "bad" moves were fantastic for the Broncos. He had one slip which ultimately ended up in them getting Peyton Manning. People may love to just look at Josh and see him go from 8-8 to 4-12 but then that's clearly not the full story and soon he's going to show people how stupid they've been for thinking he can't be a HC

Another top coordinator/HC prospect once did this and he created one of the most dominated eras in football history. He only ever had 1 winning season in the 4 years before he came to this team. While not he GM he was teaching the fresh ex-star how to be a GM and was controlling the roster because of this. I'm talking of course, of a mister Bill Belichick. He has mediocre as fuck years in Cleveland. The Patriots however had just recently made the Super Bowl, made playoffs 3 in 4 years and just barely missed the other year. However recognizing change would need to happen Kraft fired Pete Carroll and hired the Jets coordinator Belichick for a second chance and 1st round pick to their biggest rivals. Belichick immediately made big changes and the team that had so much recent success went 5-11 and had it's worst season in many years. The next year his moves created a legendary defence and won 3 SBs in 4 years and the rest is history

When you let a HC blow up the roster it should be 100% expected to have 1-2 really bad years. Because it's only ever worked out once with the '90s Cowboys. Outside of that it's never happened. The Eagles pulled a Browns-esque FO move imo and Chip Kelly will be a top coach soon for another team with hopefully an owner who actually wants to win a Super Bowl and doesn't expect one the first year after a huge rebuild
